precepts.text: Go back to the first principles of the oracles of God before you counsel anybody. The ones who qualify have their senses exercised by use — study, application, experience.
precepts.point: To be a soldier, officer, captain or deacon is to be a minister of the kingdom of God. The charge against those ministers is verse 4: they judged not aright, kept not the law themselves, walked not after the counsel of God.

precepts.text: You have need to be taught again the first principles; he that uses milk is unskillful, for he is a babe.
precepts.point: We have to come back to this Bible as a child. It is not about your age when you come to the truth; that is a carnal thing. A person can be 40 or 50 and sit among people who look younger but are spiritually older because they gained the experience of the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 131: The Weaned Child and the Milk of the Word

precepts.why:
“For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat. For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.” Some have need to be taught again the first principles; he that uses milk is unskillful in the word of righteousness, for he is a babe.

That is why we come back to this Bible as a child, quieting ourselves like a weaned child. It is not about your age when you come to the truth; that is a carnal thing. A person can be 40 or 50 and sit among people who look younger but are spiritually older, because they gained the experience of the scriptures.

points: Remember, the whole class is about training your senses to discern. Some people, they can't discern between right and wrong, good and evil. Why? Because they refuse to make this the principal thing in their life. They refuse to come around leadership to learn. Some people are just playing like they're Israelite. To me, I think it's a level of mental something wrong with you, that you come in here, put on the purple, you walk around with the fringes like you're doing it, you got a bid, but you really ain't in the mix. You're just playing a game. To me, that takes more energy than just coming to sit down and learn.

Aren't all of us looking to be great, to receive the kingdom, to rule? You can't do that if this is not important to you. You will not be able to discern between right and wrong. Somebody will come next to you and have you go to a strip club, because you can't see. Your spiritual compass is so off-kilter. I'm saying that because that happened before in a school, after breaking bread, to a brother. So you want to go to strip club? I wish you would ask me that. My question is, why would you even feel comfortable, brother? Don't do that to me. I always say that, I say that a lot: I will embarrass you. I'm telling you. But the point is, you just broke bread and then you talking about going to a strip club.

We have a brother recently in a bad place financially in his life. The Lord show him a little favour, a little blessing with a job and a car. And what do he do? He trying to pick up a. He don't have a pot to piss in nor a window to throw it out. Literally, his spiritual discernment is so far gone. He's moving with no fear. But put on a shirt and play the game. All right, let's go back. The book of Sirach chapter 39 and verse 4.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

points: Some people are dull of hearing. They can't understand or perceive. Read on.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

points: The milk is what? The laws, the basics. The strong meat is the prophecies, exercising your senses, that you can discern between right and wrong. Read on.

The reason of use is that you are exercised in the milk. Bishop Yawasap said it: deep basics. You right. That is the foundation of you growing in understanding, is to understand the small things, like keeping the commandments. Brothers want to bypass that and they want to go into prophecy, and they don't know how to deal with one another. How to apply Matthew 18 if there's an issue. How to let go of strife and beef. How to endeavour to keep the unity. How to keep a marriage together. Simple thing. How to discipline children.

We have a brother today in Austin. I just put out the body, and I hope he's listening. Disloyal, disobedient child. He's a grown man. Camp. We are trying to expand into another city. He lives in a city. We have a twenty-four to thirty-six month plan to open a school there, Lord spare life. We put a captain and some officers over that area, and we have him fourth in line there. He's in camp. I get a call. My cortisol level today was through the roof. I heard he said, Cap, tell the cap I don't agree. Are these a 60 and whatever over him? He's a 10, because he's from that. Say, I don't agree that they should be over me. I said, you got to be joking. I called, I said, put me on FaceTime. Cap, in his corner, brother. Brother walked away from him. I said, kick him out, bro. You don't get it. You don't believe the simple things, like obey them that have rule over you. That's like 101. How do we move and grow a body if you mad? You answer to the white man at the job. Why are you mad? You act like this guy's telling you to open an OnlyFans page. What are you talking about? You're too old. You got grey hair. You too old to behave like that. Men like that, we would never grow if we can't follow structure. There's structure, order, and you do what you told. We understand. You got a thousand men, flank left. Why? I got to go. Forget it. Move on. I said, we waste no time. Put him out. If you can't figure that out yet, you've been around too long to not know that. If you know better, you go home and do it. Show me how you do it. You can't discern that your actions, the ramifications, how it's going to affect your wife and your children, how it affects the greater body of Israel that we're trying to grow. David said, I'll be a doorman in the kingdom, and you jockeying for position. You mad. Nah, I wouldn't waste my time talking. Give me Sirach. What was the last thought? Discern between good and evil. Give me Sirach 34. Shame on you, bro. Shame on you. I hope you listening. Shame on you. Sirach 34:9.

points: Strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil. By reason of use: repeated practice, repeated exposure, repeated exercise. That is how the renewal works.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

points: But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.

Brothers, discerning does not come overnight. You must pray for it. You didn't become a judge because we see you can already discern; we see the potential of you becoming a great leader who eventually can discern things. As a leader, you must be able to discern certain things, and that spirit takes time. You got to pray for it over and over again, that the Most High blesses you with the spirit of discerning. Discerning can save your life; discerning can save this whole room.

There's nothing wrong with telling a brother, I'll get back to you. As men, none of us in this room knows everything. Some of you think you know everything; that's the problem. Bishop does not know everything: some of you come to Bishop asking medical questions; he's not a doctor. If the doctor prescribed it to you, go talk to the doctor.

Why does he say strong meat belongs to them that are of full age? You cannot give a baby a big piece of chicken; he's going to choke. Some of you want to learn things before your age. Learn the simple things first. A great judge starts from the bottom. It takes time to learn certain things and build yourself up. Start with Deuteronomy 28. I had a young man one time say nobody can teach him anything out of the Bible anymore. I said, okay, break down Deuteronomy 28. He couldn't even do that. This is a big book; it's going to take us a lifetime to learn it.

Stay away from big things that have nothing to do with you. The kingdom is not based on how many scriptures you know or how many deep prophecies you know. It's based on keeping the laws, keeping what the book says. You cannot do the simple thing, but you want to know the deep precepts; that makes no sense.

Video played: leadership is not a rank to be achieved; leadership is a responsibility, and it's a responsibility to see those around us rise. If you're a judge, do not keep the men around you down; build them up, if they want to be built up. But never force a man to do the work. He must willingly do the work, because when you force him, the spirit is not there.

Captain's point: the men traveling all around the world are put together in teams to do a nearly impossible task: meetings with dignitaries, school seminars, radio shows, TV shows. That's a very delicate process, and you need a certain caliber of man. When you force men to be around, they slip through the cracks; then you have to rely on that brother in a life or death situation and you find out he doesn't have the spirit on him. He was just in the vicinity, just in the room. So know the men you labor amongst, because if they're just going for a rank to be achieved without the responsibility it takes, you could end up in a very terrible situation.

The video continued: there's no CEO on the planet who's responsible for the results; you're responsible for the people, who are responsible for the people, who are responsible for the results. He just broke down the ranking system. I tell Captain the battle needs to be moved; Captain tells the men under him; the men under them tell the men under them. If at the end the battle never got moved, there was no result, and when I find out, I'm not going to look at the men at the bottom: I told Cap. And Cap is going to look at the men under him. That's how it goes. It's a difficult task, and Bishop always said black people need to learn how to work well together.

Example from Passover travel: I gave an officer responsibility over the lamb, and next thing I hear is rice and beans coming into the school for Passover. No. If you want to eat at your house before Passover, that's fine, but do not bring it here. That's why I told you: you got bishops, deacons, and captains in your camp, and you do not take advantage of it. When you go over there, these men are depending on you: show me how to do this. You have to know this thing as a judge.

Captain's point: if you're a leader and you don't have men under you coming up, that shows poor leadership skills. On the other side of the world the culture is that the men are extremely bashful; they talk very low. We asked, do you let this brother go out and teach, so he gets familiar with speaking loudly, publicly, with authority? When we did that, the brother was like a whole new man. If every Passover comes and you don't have anybody under you raising up, no man going from brother to soldier or soldier to officer, we're going to look at you, because you're supposed to be raising men up to stand in your stead. God forbid something happens to the officer in that school and nobody is built up: that school will fall unless we send men over there.

Video played of a woman executive: as a leader, you don't have to get along with everybody. The job is to lead everybody and not let your bias and your opinion get into it. It shouldn't be emotional. It's okay if you don't like every single person; the job is to respect every single person, and if you're the leader, the job is to grow every single person. If you're the judge, the job is to help every single person grow: in other words, help every single person also become a judge. The job is not to be liked.
